Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in hospitality. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

Property management system (PMS)

The source of truth for reservations, in-house guests, room status and folios. We read reservations and write profile notes through the vendor's API or interface options, never around it.

  • Oracle OPERA Cloud
  • IDS Next
  • eZee Absolute
  • Hotelogix
  • Cloudbeds
  • Mews

Channel manager and booking engine

Distributes rates and inventory to OTAs and the direct channel. Live-rate replies and rate consistency checks read from here; rate changes stay with the revenue manager.

  • STAAH
  • SiteMinder
  • eZee Centrix
  • AxisRooms
  • Hotel website booking engine

OTAs, metasearch and review platforms

Where guests discover, book and review. We work with their extranets, reports and published APIs, and respect each platform's terms.

  • Booking.com
  • MakeMyTrip and Goibibo
  • Agoda
  • Expedia
  • Google Business Profile
  • Tripadvisor

Restaurant POS and aggregator integration

Holds menus, orders, stock and payouts. Item switch-offs and daily close data move through the POS or integration partner, not by scraping partner apps.

  • Petpooja
  • Restroworks (Posist)
  • UrbanPiper
  • DotPe
  • Swiggy and Zomato partner apps

Travel booking and supplier systems

Supply flights, hotels and activities and hold the booking record. Quotes, schedule change alerts and payment schedules connect here.

  • Amadeus
  • Sabre
  • Travelport
  • TBO
  • Hotelbeds
  • Travel CRM or itinerary builder

Event, banquet and venue calendars

Hold function space, tentative holds and event details. Hold expiry reminders, proposals and run sheets read from and write back to this calendar.

  • Tripleseat
  • OPERA Cloud Sales and Event Management
  • Google Calendar
  • Microsoft Outlook calendars

Payments, accounting and statutory portals

Collect advances and instalments through hosted payment links, keep financial records, and receive statutory filings that staff submit themselves.

  • Razorpay
  • PayU
  • Stripe
  • Tally
  • Zoho Books
  • Bureau of Immigration Form III portal

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

First response time to inquiries

Median elapsed time from a new inquiry on any connected channel to the first meaningful reply by the system or a person, measured per channel and hour of day.

Why it matters: Guests contact several properties, restaurants or agencies at once, and the first useful reply often wins the booking.

Direct booking share

Room nights, covers or trips booked through the business's own channels as a share of the total for the period, by property or outlet.

Why it matters: Shows whether faster replies and consistent rates are reducing reliance on commissioned channels.

Pre-check-in completion

Arriving reservations with pre-check-in details submitted before arrival, divided by all arriving reservations that received the link.

Why it matters: Completed pre-check-in shortens the desk interaction and gives staff time to prepare rooms and extras.

Form III filings on time

Foreign guest arrivals and departures with Form III particulars submitted within twenty-four hours, as a share of all foreign guest arrivals and departures in the period.

Why it matters: It is a statutory deadline, and tracking it shows whether the desk process holds up on busy days.

Requests resolved within target

In-stay or on-trip requests closed within the agreed response target for their type, as a share of all requests in the period.

Why it matters: Shows whether requests are owned and handled during the stay or trip rather than discovered at checkout.

Review reply coverage and time

Share of new public reviews with an approved reply, and median time from review to reply, by platform and by property or outlet.

Why it matters: Considered, timely replies show prospective guests that the business listens and fixes problems.

No-show and late cancellation rate

Reservations that did not arrive or canceled inside the agreed window, divided by all reservations for the service or night.

Why it matters: Confirmations, reminders and waitlists exist to protect capacity on peak nights.

Quote and proposal turnaround

Median elapsed time from a qualified travel or event inquiry to a quote or proposal sent after a person approved it.

Why it matters: Travel and event clients compare several quotes, and turnaround affects conversion as much as price.

Wastage and stock variance

Value of recorded wastage and unexplained stock variance for key items, compared with food cost for the same outlet and period.

Why it matters: Food margins are thin, and daily visibility lets kitchens act on portioning, prep and purchasing quickly.

Settlement reconciliation exceptions

Aggregator orders or payouts that do not match the settlement statement after agreed rules are applied, counted and valued per outlet and period.

Why it matters: Unexplained deductions accumulate quietly, and a clear exception list makes disputes with aggregators possible.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
